portInfo.description: Ensenada’s cruise product is the specialised Ensenada Cruiseport Village terminal on the Bahía de Todos Santos waterfront, operated in the Hutchison Ports ECV concession and described by ASIPONA Ensenada as a cruise dock with customs/migration module, two gangways and two berthing positions. ASIPONA states operating capacity for vessels up to 3,200 passengers and a projected 800,000 passengers per year; the same page’s update stamp is 14 May 2015, so treat capacity figures as dated until a newer official year is found. Pier lengths and depths disagree slightly between ASIPONA and Hutchison — both are cited, neither door GPS is invented.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Ensenada Cruiseport Village — Pier / Dock 1 — Blvd. Costero S/N, Zona Centro, 22800 Ensenada, Baja California, México
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Centro. Terminal sits on Blvd. Costero in Zona Centro. Published walking minutes from gangway to Malecón gate are not on the cited official pages — treat as unverified. Transfers. Port shuttle/taxi arrangements vary by call; not inventoried here. From US border. Road distance/time from San Diego not used as a cruise-day fact.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Zona Centro / Malecón waterfront near the harbour — ~90 min.
Local market / Avenida López Mateos corridor — hours and named shops not verified on primary pages used here.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Reconcile which ECV pier you are on before planning LOA/draft assumptions — ASIPONA and Hutchison publish different pier lengths and depths for the same two docks.
